title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: the forest years are over, and Yudhishthira asks each brother and Draupadi a plain question: what will you be?
carry: every disguise is built from something real

segments.voice: Yesterday: Dharma, the voice at the lake, revealed as Yudhishthira's own father, after a choice that kept the family fair. Your line was the one who keeps the family fair.

One last year, lived among people, without being recognized. Those were the terms of the dice game, and if anyone sees through them, the exile begins again. So the five brothers and Draupadi sit together, and Yudhishthira asks each of them a question. Not where will you hide. What will you be? Where will you work, and as whom? They have chosen a kingdom to vanish into: the land of the Matsyas, ruled by King Virata. The Virata book opens with something close to a job interview, held in secret.
screen: `ONE YEAR, UNRECOGNIZED.` → `WHAT WILL YOU BE?` → `THE COURT OF KING VIRATA.`

segments.voice: Each answer tells you something. Yudhishthira goes first. He will be Kanka, a Brahmin who plays dice with the king and keeps him company. Stop on that. The man whose love of dice cost them everything chooses dice as his cover. Bhima will be Vallava, the cook, and he'll wrestle if the court wants a show. The brother with the famous appetite will run the kitchen. Arjuna has a harder problem: the scars a bowstring leaves on a warrior's arms. He'll hide them under bangles and live as Brihannala, a eunuch who teaches singing and dance to the women of the palace. Nakula will keep the king's horses. Sahadeva will keep the cattle. And Draupadi, a queen, will serve the queen as Sairandhri, a maid who dresses hair. Nobody pretends to a skill they don't have. Every disguise is built from something real. The rank is hidden. The person isn't. Then their priest, Dhaumya, gives them advice for life in a king's house, and it reads like advice for a first week at any new job. Don't take a seat that might belong to someone else. Speak when you're asked. Don't show off, and don't gossip about the king's private affairs. Be useful, and be quiet about it. The great heroes of the epic are about to spend a year as staff.
screen: `EACH ONE ASKED: WHAT WILL YOU BE?` · `THE DICE MAN CHOOSES DICE` · `EVERY DISGUISE BUILT ON A REAL SKILL` · then, large: `DHAUMYA: HOW TO LIVE AT COURT`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one role you play, at work, at home or among friends, and as you breathe in, ask what that role asks of you. As you breathe out, find the real skill underneath it, patience, a good ear, steady hands, and stay with it for a few breaths, the way Bhima's cooking sat under the name Vallava. If you pray, you can offer that skill in your prayer.
Virata. The king of the Matsyas, whose court will hide the Pandavas and Draupadi for their year in disguise.
Your line: every disguise is built from something real. A dice player, a cook, a dance teacher, two herders and a maid. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 807 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.`

howItsDone: The Virata book is read and retold as part of the Mahabharata, and the disguises the Pandavas choose (Kanka, Vallava, Brihannala, Sairandhri) are familiar names from retellings and performances of the epic.

fork.setup: you're Yudhishthira. dice cost you your kingdom. now you need a disguise for a royal court. what do you choose?
options: a guard at the palace gate.
a Brahmin who plays dice with the king.
a hermit who stays outside the city.
fork.reveal: he becomes Kanka, the king's dice companion. the very game that ruined him becomes his cover.

original.note: the king of the Matsyas; his name titles this book of the epic, the Virata Parva.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Pandavas simply went into hiding.
what it means: each chose a working life built on a real skill, hiding rank but not the person.
what a scholar hears: some readers hear the Virata book as a book of reversals: a king as courtier, a warrior as dancer, a queen as maid.

chat.says: Why does Yudhishthira pick dice as his disguise, after dice cost them everything?
options: Each of them chose a cover built on a real skill, and dice was his.
He planned to win their kingdom back from Virata in a secret game.
Dhaumya told him a dice player would never be noticed at court.
chat.meaning: Kanka the dice player, Vallava the cook, Brihannala the dance teacher: every disguise rests on something real. The rank is hidden, not the person.

Virata.meaning: king of the Matsyas, in whose court the Pandavas hide

Sairandhri.meaning: Draupadi's disguise: a maid who dresses the queen's hair

Dhaumya.meaning: the Pandavas' family priest, who advises them on life at court
